sources_say.text: Novo Nordisk's Q1 presentation describes AMAZE 2 as an 84-week placebo-controlled study, with weight loss as its primary endpoint, in people with type 2 diabetes.
Its Q2 presentation retains that description and labels project timelines as directional.
The August financial report discusses other zenagamtide trials, HF-POLARIS and AMAZE 8, rather than explaining this AMAZE 2 date revision.

unclear: Does this affect the results-release schedule?

analyst_view: [Inference] This warrants tracking the timing of AMAZE 2 evidence, with moderate confidence in its monitoring importance.
[Inference] Confidence in any cause or competitive impact is low; this revision alone cannot establish a setback in efficacy, safety, or launch timing relative to competitors.

runs.importance_note: Recruitment for Amgen's largest MariTide trial closed about 15 months after it started; the planned completion dates did not move.

what_happened.text: Version 32 changed Overall Status from Recruiting to Active, not recruiting; it was submitted on October 27 and posted on October 29, 2026.
Nothing else tracked changed: enrollment stayed at 12,800 (estimated), primary completion at June 30, 2028 and study completion at September 29, 2030 (both estimated), with 783 listed sites.
The record gives July 25, 2025 as the actual study start.

sources_say.text: Amgen's third-quarter results release of November 3, 2026 says MARITIME-CV "has completed enrollment" of adults with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and obesity or overweight.
The same release says the two sleep-apnea trials (MARITIME-OSA-1 and -2) have also completed enrollment, MARITIME-HF is still enrolling, and MARITIME-1 and -2 are ongoing.
The release gives no enrolled-participant count, no date on which enrollment closed, and no timing for MARITIME-CV results.

unclear: How many participants were actually enrolled? The registry still shows 12,800 as an estimate.
On what date did enrollment close?
When does Amgen expect cardiovascular outcome results?
analyst_view: [Inference] The status change reflects completed enrollment. Confidence is high: the company said so one week after the registry update, naming the same trial.
[Inference] With recruitment closed, the timing of results now depends on follow-up rather than on finding patients. Confidence is moderate, because Amgen has not stated a results date.

[Inference] For competitors, this keeps MariTide's cardiovascular evidence on its registered schedule (primary completion mid-2028). Confidence is low to moderate, because registry dates are estimates.

what_happened.text: Version 9 changed Overall Status from Recruiting to Active, not recruiting, and enrollment from 630 to 638 (still marked estimated); it was submitted on November 5 and posted on November 6, 2026.
Estimated primary completion and study completion both stayed at August 7, 2028; listed sites went from 74 to 73.

sources_say.text: Novo Nordisk's nine-month report of November 4, 2026 lists newly started zenagamtide trials (AMAZE 9, AMAZE 7, AMAZE 10, AMBITION 7 and AMBIENCE) but says nothing about AMAZE 2 recruitment, participant numbers or timing. The appendices after Appendix 2 were not read.
The second-quarter investor presentation describes AMAZE 2 as an 84-week placebo-controlled trial of weight loss in people with type 2 diabetes, and calls project timelines directional.

unclear: Is 638 the final number of participants? The registry still marks it as estimated.
Did recruitment end because the target was reached?
Does the end of recruitment change when results are expected?
analyst_view: [Inference] Recruitment most likely finished slightly above the 630 target. Confidence is moderate: this rests on the registry alone, with no company statement.
[Inference] The unchanged August 2028 date gives no sign of a timeline shift. Confidence is low to moderate, because registry dates are estimates.
[Inference] This change alone says nothing about efficacy, safety or position against competitors.

sources_say.text: Lilly's third-quarter 2026 earnings presentation lists this trial as Phase 2 with 200 patients, percent change in body weight as the primary outcome, and primary completion in March 2027; the slide cites ClinicalTrials.gov as of October 20, 2026.
Its pipeline slide, dated October 27, 2026, lists macupatide plus eloralintide for obesity, and the deck makes no statement about enrollment or data timing for this trial.
The same slide lists a second, larger Phase 2 trial of the combination (NCT07589608, 400 patients) with primary completion in September 2027.

unclear: Did recruitment end because the 200-patient target was reached? Enrollment is still marked estimated.
When will Lilly report results from this trial?
analyst_view: [Inference] Recruitment most likely completed about a year after the trial started. Confidence is moderate: this rests on the registry alone.
[Inference] First weight-loss data for the combination in people with type 2 diabetes could follow the March 2027 primary completion. Confidence is low, because Lilly has not given a date.
[Inference] This change alone says nothing about efficacy, safety or position against competitors.
